56afd259-0505-5d2d-b7f1-9be15cb0dea2.definition: Arabic dynasty that initially ruled over most of the Islamic empire after assuming the caliphate in 750 CE.

e2af48f9-49cb-51b7-84fd-bbcca177f07b.definition:
Masonry technique used in facades of historical buildings and characterised by alternating rows of light (yellow or white) and dark (red or black) stones or bricks.  
  
The first fortress built in this style in northern Arabia during the 5th century AD was the fortress of Samawal. The style spread from al-Andalus, specifically from the Great Mosque of Cordoba (AH 170 / AD 776) into Islamic architecture. It became popular in the Levant due to the availability of white limestone and black basalt. A notable example is the Azem (or Ablaq) Palace in Damascus. Examples in Cairo include Khanqah Baybars al-Jashankir and the mosque built by Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.

199be476-a6fb-5584-8c39-6af25455b9be.definition: A paper-treating process. Paper that was to be used for calligraphy had to be treated to prevent the ink from spreading. The paper was sized (*ahar*) with a special solution to obtain a very smooth surface.

34f3c711-7719-5478-a311-2b54051f81d0.definition: One of the 99 names of God, meaning The Just, fair.

c44302b7-5b2a-5247-b1b7-8c1a06993aa4.definition: The 2nd Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Cow". It is composed of 286 verses.

9c2e2004-3d90-5af9-823b-a7e2d698d965.definition: The 3rd Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Family of Irman". It is composed of 200 verses.

3d741e10-844b-53b3-bd76-b7ab36e8c586.definition: The 4th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Women". It is composed of 176 verses.

782abace-0002-5e80-8b1f-a5cb1d7a353a.definition: The 9th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Repentance". It is composed of 129 verses.

16131753-740a-5b87-bfb9-06606e67de19.definition: A flag, banner or standard. They were carried next to a commander in a military campaign or were used in religious processions. They could be very different in shape and had geometric designs, sometimes with inscriptions. A metal *alem* could be mounted to the head of a pole.

d622d348-fe31-5163-9440-a84a07e7456c.definition: (Pl. *‘ulama’*) Scholar, doctor of law and Islamic theological science. Fr: ouléma or uléma. Tr: alim, pl. ulema.

fb4643f3-3421-5aaa-8b4f-85806f394bac.definition: A designation for a two-dimensional ornamental pattern in Islamic art. Arabesques are constructed designs based on intertwined leaf stems and tendrils that create a continuous pattern sometimes in connection with scrolls or geometrical elements.

983e0813-bc71-581c-82c8-e8186f09992d.definition: A row of shops aligned along a street, which may be covered or open. See also *bazaar*, *bedesten*, *qaysariyya*, *suq*.

13b13347-73d9-5e9b-896e-e43453a70910.definition: (pl. of *rabat*). In Sufi tradition, an *arbita refers to a hospice combined with an educational establishment.*

f80f3b72-49a9-5057-bd6f-021ba24a6071.definition: A medieval scientific instrument used for astronomical calculations and navigation.

1967d28e-68f6-5e68-b680-9a66e81477fb.definition: Commander-in-chief of the armies. Atabegs were appointed as tutors for young Seljuq princes acting as governors of important towns but they gained power and in time their independence.

f8abb38d-e51e-5fc5-9493-dc1508482dcf.definition: Plural of Wakf, meaning religious endowments. Also meaning endowments.

8383edc1-0cb4-52fa-9e3a-219b3a940129.definition: (Pl. *ayat*) Verse in the Qur’an. Tr. ayet.

ac67e975-1f75-526f-a8cd-402ccde93f6f.definition: A formula, *bi-‘ism Allah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, which is commonly translated as “In the name of God, the Clement, the Merciful”. Fr. *besmala*; Tr. *besmele*.

b8c40deb-d541-5941-870e-bbb5a22c7520.definition: (Pl. *biyut*) Room; in certain cases a house. *baytal-Hikma*: tribunal. *bayt ad-diwan*: reception hall. *bayt al-nar*: furnace, literally “house of the fire”. See also *dar*, *qasr*.

816929a9-190c-57b7-8bc6-469a25050fac.definition: The ruler of an independent emirate; a title of respect for a man of the upper classes; title held by the sovereign vassals of the sultan. *Beylerbeyi*: The bey of beys: the highest rank in the provincial government of the Ottoman Empire. *Beylicat*, *beylik*: soverignty of or territory ruled by a bey. See also *agha*, *dey*.

53b06a4c-1741-53c4-bd23-415aa3ce7613.definition: Fort, bastion, tower, sometimes surrounded by an outer wall. The term passed into mediaeval Portuguese toponymy as *alvorge* or porches. In Tunisia it also means a secondary residence surrounded by gardens; a pleasure palace. Maghreb *borj*. Egypt *burg*. Tr. *burç*.

b3b18f28-32c7-5836-ae64-e0df239443e1.definition: The Byzantine empire (306 to 1453) which was preceded by the Roman empire and succeeded by the Ottoman Empire.

b6c3a09c-964b-5dd3-a091-e608967fe6ff.definition: Ar. *khalifa* literally “successor”. The supreme head of the Muslim community. Caliphate: the territory under the power of the caliph.

c2953466-916b-57e9-9f3b-409c9af9afa1.definition: The “art of beautiful writing” (Greek) is one of the highest artforms of Islamic culture. As the Arabic language is connected with the revelation of Islam, calligraphy has deep spiritual undertones and is valued as a symbol of beauty and mystery. There are many types of calligraphy with variations according to period, place and context. Many artists of the Arab and Muslim world continue to practise calligraphy today. See also *diwani*, *farsi*, *kufic*, Maghribi-Andalusi, *muhaqqaq*, *naskhi*, *nasta’liq*, *rayhani*, *ruq’a*, *ta’liq*, *thuluth*.

801f574d-c2f6-52a3-ae7c-6a0074f1c59b.definition: From Persian. Hostel along main travelling routes to accommodate travellers and safeguard their goods. See also *funduq*, *khan*, *wikala*.

90c8aeb0-fee7-5ad8-b2e8-525f87d18e3a.definition: Fortress, citadel, usually equated with the city centre. Ar. *qasba*. *Ksiba*: small kasbah, the name of a neighbourhood in Bizerte, Tunisia. See also *hisn*, *qal’a*.

4a12c207-113d-5b87-992e-9db5d88374f3.definition: The first Muslim societies continued to use Byzantine solidus gold coins and Sassanian silver dirhams. In time, Qur'anic phrases, place of minting, names of caliph and sultan and Hijri date were added. With the Umayyad coinage revolution in AH 696–7 / AD 1296–7, pure epigraphic coins came into use. Akche: silver coin, basic unit of Ottoman money system; dinar: gold coin, equal to 10 dirhams; fils: copper coin.

44562f82-b0b6-5353-939a-47fccfb7fa3c.definition: Sacred text of the Islamic Revelation transmitted by the Archangel Gabriel to the Prophet Muhammad. From the root *qr*’, “to recite, to read”.

f3052f85-4db5-5572-a790-f3dc9a248659.definition: (Pl. *dur*) House. *Dar al-imara*: Governor’s house. Dar al-Islam: Domain of Islam: countries under Islamic rule; where Islam did not rule was considered war territory. *Dar al-Hadith*: A school for studying the Hadith; Tr. *Darülhadis*. *Dar al-Hijra*: Abode for migration. *Dar al-khuffaz*: A school for training of memorising the Qur’an; Tr. *Darülhuffaz*. Dar al-Qurra’: school for teaching Qur’an recitation as a science ; Tr. *Darülkurra*. *Dar al-shifa’*: hospital; Tr. *darüşşifa*. *Dar al-tibb*: A school where the medical sciences were taught; Tr. *Darüttıb*. See also *bayt*, *qasr*.

0b0c9320-1a31-574f-aa24-7c9a581717b2.definition: Alleyway, route. In Morocco and Tunisia derb: alley or by extension a neighbourhood. *Darb al-Hajj*: route taken to Mecca by pilgrims from every corner of the Islamic world. Usually all necessary services, especially security, were provided by the administration. Caravans would meet at specified times in designated places, e.g. the Turkish caravan would meet the caravan from al-Sham and they would travel together to join the Jordanian and Palestinian caravans.

b64a1f79-8f29-5ad4-8e98-379f8e05cb1b.definition: Member of a Muslim religious order noted for its devotional practices. Fr. *derviche*.

31591fdd-18fb-5898-b2ac-33ccb03797c8.definition: A place with a very small population in the state and region of Amman Governorate in Jordan.

eb4ec166-81db-5b55-9f7c-de12b453b102.definition: The term dhikr comes from the triliteral root that means "to remember". In the context of the Islamic tradition, dhikr means the remembrance of God. This remembrance of God can take many forms. The word dhikr is also used to mean litanies and specific phrases in remembrance of God. This term could mean the Quran.

f68bb09f-0323-528e-a7bc-c97eec5531d8.definition: Monetary unit used in several countries. It was first introduced as an Islamic coinage in the late 7th century CE by Abd al-Malik of the Umayyad dynasty. The dinar dates from the Roman times, when it was known as denarius. Made of gold.

3230cdd8-ec0e-5aa1-9b44-adc5716d86b8.definition: An office of government; audience hall, reception chamber; a collection of poems. Tr. divan; divan-ı Hümayun: the Imperial Council, chaired by the Grand Vizier, forming the central organ of the Ottoman government.

476a1ad7-f594-57bd-8ef5-ddfe4dba9e8b.definition: A lacquer technique first seen in Iran in the AH 9th / AD 15th century during the Timurid period. It was named after Edirne in Turkey from where the best examples came. It was used on different media such as bindings, drawers and bows.

8f750e3f-a3f4-5b39-8f9c-97cbf1eb56ec.definition: A military commander, prince or senior official; the ruler of an emirate or principality; Tr. *emir*. amir akhur: *amir* responsible for sultan’s stables, camels and postal service; Tr. *emir* *ahur* or imrahor. amir al-Mu’minin: Prince of Believers; Tr. *emirü’l-müminin*. amir al-Muslimin: Prince of Muslims; Tr. *emirü’l-müslimin*. amir al-silah: *amir* responsible for arms. amir kabir: Great Amir. Fr. *émir*.

cd62ef51-dfea-5e66-a924-b9ac8fd72a21.definition: A French term for maiolica, tin-glazed earthenware of post-Medieval Europe. Also a ceramic composed of a body of crushed quartz and an overlying glaze, common in the ancient Near East and Mediterranean. Capable of being moulded into small objects which were initially confused with earthenware with a white tin glaze and the term faience, incorrectly applied, has remained in use.

3fd5d8e5-d6d9-5084-a7bc-f270946f8c24.definition:
"Farsi" refers to the Persian language. It is primarily spoken in Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan and is written in the Persian script.  
  
1\. An inhabitant of Persia. 2. Cursive, particularly elegant calligraphic style which emphasises the curves of the Arabic letters by reducing the angular figures. See also calligraphy.

38f9b696-41fe-5bb6-aea9-f97476afeed6.definition:
This term has different meanings:  
  
Fez  
City in northern Morocco  
  
Fez  
A brimless cylindrical or somewhat cone-shaped hat with a flat top that usually has a tassel, is typically made of red felt, and is worn especially by men in eastern Mediterranean countries

720487c1-6546-5ad8-96ce-6caedac4ddab.definition: A leaf with illustration preceding the title-page of a book.

09e9e553-3757-50e9-a411-6aaea263cdac.definition: The so-called Turkish knot in a pile rug or carpet. Another term is symmetrical knot or double knot. The asymmetrical knot exists in Persian carpets, called a Senneh knot.

e0e8a76f-5937-523a-b87b-6d2a0c6528d7.definition: Applying gold to the surface of an artwork. Gilding can be applied to most materials, including marble, stone, stucco, wood, metalwork, ceramics, glass and paper. Different techniques are used to apply gold, as it can be applied in a light wash or as gold-leaf foil. Tr. *tombak*, gilded copper technique.

2fb79a2a-639b-5703-9b25-ab627b16aef8.definition: A gift of real estate bequeathed in perpetuity under certain conditions in favour of a mosque or other religious institution, such as a *madrasa* or *khanqah*, or a civil institution such as a *sabil*, or even a house. See also *waqf*.

c18561f3-9ed2-5c21-92a7-c3476d781d57.definition: Literally, “sayings”. Body of traditions related to the sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad and his companions. *Dar al-Hadith*: see *dar*.

4a7c27f5-2059-522b-a21e-ee99a0c6ac00.definition: A high government official. The term originally designated a chamberlain, but under the Spanish Umayyads the *hajib* functioned as a chief minister, paralleling the position of vizier in the eastern caliphates.

cccf5396-0f64-5785-9f34-bb8b7a5ffd5b.definition: One of the five pillars of Islam: pilgrimage to Mecca and holy places, which all believers must accomplish at least once during their lifetime if they have the means to do so. By extension it also refers to someone who undertakes the pilgrimage. Hajj takes place two months after Ramadan and finishes with the Feast of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha). ‘Umra has almost the same rituals as the Hajj but takes place outside the Hajj season. ‘Umra’s significance is growing because there is no means to house the increasingly large numbers (over three million) who want to go on Hajj.

fc74d5ab-7517-53a5-9a58-0cb34c65fec8.definition: Public or private bathhouse. Apodyterium: changing room; Tr. *soyunmalık*. Caldarium: hot room. Hypocaust: floor and wall heating system by steam in Roman baths and villas. Tepidarium: warm room where bathers would rest after bathing; Tr. *ılıklık*. Also in Turkish bathhouse: *aralık*: passageway between the *soyunmalık* and *ılıklık*; *halvet*: private chambers in a public bath; *traşlık*: small room used for the removal of body hair. Also in Syrian bathhouse: *barrani* (lit. “exterior”): the cold room of a bathhouse because it is usually located furthest from the furnace; *juwwani*: most interior part, closest to furnace – steam room; *wustani*: middle chambers designated as the “warm water chambers”. See also *maqsura*.

cc92b83e-cb72-55df-b6de-8ddaf5a44e3f.definition: One of the four Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. Tr. Hanbeli. See also *fiqh’*.

d71360cd-eac1-5408-b6b3-59ad3d8464b9.definition: Ar. literally “sacred”, “forbidden”. Sanctuary. An illicit act from the religious point of view. Haram al-Sharif: the Noble Sanctuary in Jerusalem including al-Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock.

0ad8de69-3a63-53bc-8e1b-4c6cae853bca.definition: Common living space in a Turkish house. Tr. also *sofa*.

0f3fb66d-a491-591b-a0c2-56e11ec481aa.definition: Muhammad’s flight from Mecca to Madina in AD 622. The beginning of the Muslim Hijri (Hegira) calendar, which follows a lunar year.

dcd58376-8ba5-5488-bec0-53d4cf2fa497.definition: A prose description of the Prophet Muhammad. Hilya-i Sharif: noble description of the prophet, a work of art bearing the noble description.

d741661c-846f-560d-a11c-19720819ac9a.definition: Son of, used in names. To indicate a clan the plural form *Bani / Banu*. is used. Tr. –*oğlu*.

441e3156-be30-517c-a195-12e2d3486ed8.definition: One who presides over Islamic prayers, a guide, chief, spiritual model or cleric; sometimes also a political leader in Muslim society.

7fb96b21-abb1-5f60-883e-2d6e33ce522d.definition: This is a term in Swahili meaning flourishing, strong.

d92f6fd0-31e4-5a3e-a04f-1708743e899b.definition: From Ar. *imara*. A complex of buildings and institutions supported by a *waqf*. After the AH 10th / AD 16th century a public soup-kitchen for the poor.

1bcff5a5-1586-5d9e-a84e-b16a4a88bdae.definition: The Prophet Muhammad’s midnight journey from Mecca to Jerusalem.

ed1392a3-c2e4-5dca-8b74-eaef4f0f9c94.definition: A vaulted hall or domed hall, walled on three sides with a large opening arch. Tr. eyvan.

070e713b-f503-5f87-be41-16cb73c070b4.definition: Main mosque where daily prayers and Friday prayers are celebrated. Tr. *cami*. See also *meşrebiye*.

2003ec95-a720-51cb-9dcd-774d9dc9f389.definition: The text of the Qur’an can be divided into 30 equal sections. One-thirtieth is therefore called a *juz’* (pl. ajza). When Qur’ans were written in 30 volumes, as in Mamluk Egypt, one volume was a *juz’*.

98afafd6-f8b6-5d37-923e-752f4697a5a7.definition: Literally “cube”. Temple in Mecca, the centre of the Islamic religion.

04f42d3e-3607-5497-ac48-4aa51fe765d3.definition: A small room or cell (sometimes an independent building) with few or no windows to which Sufis retreat. It corresponds to the *halvet* of a Turkish bath – see *hammam*.

cf7d3667-7d96-58e6-af31-c5d6fe2c71b8.definition: Ar. Inn, lodgings on the main caravan routes for travellers (pilgrims and merchants) and where merchandise could be stored. See also *caravanserai*, *funduq*, *wikala*. Tr. *han*.

1863aa1c-4cad-53d2-a497-ecb16318e81f.definition: Monastery or hostel for itinerant Sufis or dervishes. Tr. *hanikah*, *hankah*. See also *zawiya*.

53d47884-ba36-5979-a58f-ff35b0bd8587.definition: A cloth composed of different parts to cover the Ka’ba in Mecca. It is embroidered in silk and gold with Qur’anic verses. A new one is made each year. The change takes places during the Hajj, when the old *kiswa* is cut up and distributed among the people. Cloths with zigzag patterns of calligraphy that cover mausolea cenotaphs are also called *kiswa* (e.g. in Palestine).

95fc5a14-1b29-5364-810a-69fc76087256.definition:
An Arabic script of angular and stylised characters used in Qur’ans in the early period of Islam. It is attributed to the city of Kufa in Iraq. From the AH 4th / AD 10th century it was less used because it could be difficult to read. Foliated *kufic*: a script that combines the angular style of the letters with decorative floral and vegetal motifs as finials, popular during the Fatimid and Atabeg period. See also calligraphy.  
  
Kufic script emerged as an Arabic script style, initially rising to prominence as the favoured choice for transcribing the Qurʾan and adorning architectural structures. Over time, it evolved into a point of reference and an exemplary model for various other Arabic scripts. Kufic script is characterised by its markedly angular form within the Arabic alphabet, originating in the initial copies of the Qurʾan.

81dc2164-deae-5d1f-8a05-4e038d6354b1.definition: An Ottoman Turkish term that refers to religious and charitable complexes comprising several buildings with the mosque is at the centre. The other buildings were the hospital, bathhouse, soup-kitchen *darüşşifa* (hospital), *hammam* (bathhouse), *han* (lodgings), *imaret* (soup-kitchen), *madrasa* (school).

6d80067a-11d1-5a05-8e27-1c1e30ff12b0.definition: Word used for chair or throne, depending on the context.

220ac6c9-5bbb-5494-a7d7-a1992e0113c3.definition: A ceramic technique in which a thin coating of metal oxide resulted in an iridescent and golden shining surface on glazed ceramics. The lustre technique was introduced to many different regions by travelling potters.

ff94889d-f66f-5e04-bc88-5fba2822cea4.definition: Location in southern Jordan, located 218 km from the capital Amman.

de7865d2-5988-5b78-b69f-32fb1986c355.definition: A defensive architectural feature found on the exterior of towers and gates used to pour hot oil onto enemies below. Ar. saqqata from the root *s q t*, “to drop”.

455c1318-16a9-50f2-9c44-6643a9de238c.definition:
Theological institution that provided instruction on Islamic law (*shari’a*), jurisprudence (*fiqh*), Quran, Hadith, and Arabic, as well as accomodations for students.  
  
Today, a school. Fr. *medersa*, Tr. *medrese*.

bd6ee598-f323-5770-a786-0151295aea83.definition: One of the four Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. Founded by Imam Malik and spread throughout the western Muslim world including al-Andalus.

af45d65f-d61d-59ed-bd55-76ee503119e9.definition: Building of one or more architectural units, usually with a dome, that contains the tomb of an important religious figure. A place of worship, and pilgrimage. See also darih, *mashhad*, *qubba*, *türbe*.

f2ec79dc-0998-56d5-8cc2-bce2d4228e77.definition:
Building of one or more architectural units, usually with a dome, that contains the tomb of an important religious figure. A place of worship, and pilgrimage. See also darih, mashhad, qubba, türbe.  
Additionally, Mashhad, alternatively spelled as Mashad or Meshed, serves as the city and capital of the Khorasan-e Razavi province in north-eastern Iran.  
  
See also darih, *maqam*, *qubba*, *türbe*.

3bcfdeb5-5c8a-58e9-8dfd-9ad2a9f98fdb.definition: Wooden lattice screens made of turned pieces of wood assembled to form a window grille. Fr: *machrabiyya*. Tr. *meşrebiye*.

f176a992-6546-55ba-a3e5-6877adc61b76.definition: Literally, “place of prostration”. A mosque where daily prayers are held, usually with the exception of the Friday prayers, which cannot take place in a *meşrebiye* owing to the absence of a *minbar*. Tr. *mescit*. See also *jami’*.

a04d4101-e499-5fb8-ad85-ae402c6b673f.definition: A long stone protruding ledge or bench against an outer wall on either side of entrance to a building.

e99f9b90-c624-5aa1-815f-a47f478f7da3.definition: Town, the old quarter, self-sufficient city centre. Also the name of a city in Saudi Arabia where the Muslims migrated in AD 622 and where the Prophet Muhammad is buried.

32178605-4854-58d8-b7b4-f35cf3cf68f4.definition: Ascension of the Great Prophet Muhammad to Heaven to the throne of Allah, where he received the divine instruction for the five daily prayers (*salat*) for Muslims. Along with Muhammad’s night journey *Isrāʾ from the “sacred place of worship” (Mecca) to the “further place of worship” (Jerusalem), the Mi’raj creates the two parts of the night journey of Muhammad.*

e7f7d170-9ce3-5eb5-8c00-b201155164d8.definition: Arched niche, usually concave but sometimes flat, in religious Islamic buildings indicating the direction of Mecca, which worshippers face when praying.

a7da3b34-cced-5cac-bca5-7cde2160fdbf.definition: A stepped pulpit for delivering the sermon during the Friday prayers and the first morning prayers during the two big Muslim feasts. It is placed to the right of the *mihrab* in a mosque. *minbar*s first appeared in the Umayyad period.

b2f40fe6-7d9e-55fe-91fd-b02fa7f5b5a2.definition: In the Christian kingdoms of the Peninsula the name given to Muslims who formally converted to Christianity after the Reconquista.

a26fcbf5-43f5-53e6-8d77-b2efc78c5302.definition: Funerary stele which is usually made out of marble. Mqabriya is an equivalent of a tomb stone.

b9deabe4-38f9-5144-9eed-f59423fe7ddc.definition: Muslim religious official charged with announcing from the mosque minaret the five prayers of the day. *Müezzin mahfili*: Tr., special platform for the *muezzin*s. See also *adhan*.

cfc9414f-7ca4-5e8a-80ea-d0fc4865d5c9.definition: From Ar. *muwallad*. Christians who were converted to Islamism and lived as Muslims during the domination of the Arabs in the Iberian Peninsula.

bd2ffd1a-1d12-5fc1-ab6b-b186e0622cb6.definition: Stalactite- or honeycomb-like architectural ornamentation which adorns many surfaces including domes and corbels. In the Maghreb *muqarbas*. Fr. *mouqarnas*.

b43d4539-8c8e-5de3-ba56-a72f1632c7c8.definition: Meaning "bitter", often used to describe coffee.

8ffa05a8-a165-5e2c-b72e-27e8d5f953ac.definition: Literally “copied”. One of the most widespread styles of Islamic calligraphy used in Qur’ans and other books. It combines the flexibility of the *farsi* style with the harmony of the *kufic* script. Tr. *nesih*.

ea9e06ca-7872-5541-9ac2-11302f8890c2.definition: A Turkish honorific title, arabicised as *Basha*.

60068ca4-be84-58d0-a590-341306ae5e41.definition: Pearls, the only organic material considered to be precious gemstones, can be widely divided into two categories: natural and cultivated. The formation of the pearl occurs when a foreign body such as a grain of sand or a parasite enters the shell of an oyster or mussel. Due to their very specific origin, pearls have come to be focal points of many legends and myths. Because of their circular shape, they are frequently associated with the moon. They can also symbolize life in general, as well as birth. Some old beliefs state that morning dew, when hardened, turns into pearls. Civilizations from areas with pearl fishing cultures, such as the Middle East and Asia, have for centuries viewed pearls as symbols of supremacy, innocence and female charm.

dc0561a2-2592-560f-8a87-20cd58a96753.definition:
"Chest Panel  
From the head of the right shoulder to the end of the left shoulder."

59b4beee-e4d9-52ef-99f1-2a66945a3694.definition: A term for glazed tile panels derived from the Iranian city of Kashan, where tiles to decorate buildings had been produced since the Seljuq period. The term was used by the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battutah in Iran for the tile panels that reminded him of the *zellij* tiles of the Maghreb.

c47920b0-c22e-53d0-aa8c-93eb3956ca0e.definition: From Latin *castrum*. Palace, castle. *Qusayr*: diminutive form of *qasr*. Tr. kasr. See also *bayt*, dar.

0089ce74-d5cd-57d2-bbe4-c8de79b156c9.definition: Direction of the Ka‘ba in Mecca, which Muslims face during prayer. The qibla wall of the mosque is where the *mihrab* is situated.

ea03a56c-d809-5ee0-9bf3-d2601be89fe3.definition: A portable astronomical instrument whose name literally means "showing the direction to the Ka'ba". The alternative name for it is astrolabe.

c39cd815-3b51-5b89-a4e4-5e9f2c0ca622.definition: Dome; by extension a monument or chamber built over the grave of a saint or important person, which is usually marked with a dome. Fr. *koubba*. Tr. *kubbe* (dome only).

9c6aeb81-7bc2-5ea4-9209-1c4a1345ac29.definition: The division of the Qur’an into 30 parts. Each part (*juz’*) was bound as a separate volume and usually the 30 volumes were housed in an illuminated box.

44b5dcf7-b45d-5206-b3e1-f77d5f220d80.definition: A metalworking technique. To make a design appear in relief on the front of a metal work of art, it has to be worked in repoussé (hammered) from the back.

9a8096ea-a204-590a-8744-2ddf28c2b6b8.definition: Fortified enclosure for religious warriors (North Africa); a hospice for pilgrims (Mamluk Egypt, Palestine and Syria). The name of the town Rabat comes from Ribat al-Fath (Ribat of the Conquest).

99e11148-863b-5916-afb5-d3b71fb5abe5.definition: Split-palmette motif. One of the most popular and basic motifs in Islamic decorative arts, applied to every medium from woodcarving to tiles. It is mostly seen in arabesques. It was named after an earlier name for Anatolia.

a8525513-1742-5e9f-85de-bb2067ad9fb6.definition:
(Pl. *subul* or *asbila*) Small structures that were designed to dispense and provide free and clean drinking water to the public. *Sabil*s can be freestanding buildings or parts of small or large charitable complexes.  
  
Tr. sebil – a chamber where an attendant serves free drink to the public.

7b0b0e45-2f2a-5fd0-be86-16fa0e895a59.definition: In the Maghreb an entrance to a house, often twisting and turning.

0f26046e-3b67-5601-baf6-72d291d77ad0.definition: Straight, double-edged sword. The sayf varied in appearance throughout Islamic history.

98f32a82-0f8d-523b-b82b-b4c5d2090590.definition: (Pl. *sada*) Descendants of Prophet Muhammad. See also *sharif*.

9ba68a24-0e40-52cc-9957-968da7055d9a.definition: Arabic title of respect, meaning Heir to the grandson of the prophet Muhammad.

11864cd8-7574-5b81-8dbd-f0180dc203cf.definition: The writer of *Şehname*, equivalent to a court historian.

1e2bc98b-db88-5155-9556-2e6e52c00a36.definition: Mobile openwork plaque or rete, could also mean net.

bd727956-74e1-5614-9f39-07003f768b6a.definition: Literally, “road”. Islamic precepts that the believer must follow in order to be on the right road that leads to God. The *Shari‘a* rules the behaviour of the faithful in the spiritual, legal, social and political spheres, and also in the concrete aspects of daily life.

a0a0b21a-5425-5de1-8d04-b7fd7daeca8b.definition: An elder, respected for his knowledge and age, learned man instructed in the religious sciences, member of a religious brotherhood, sufi master. Tr. *Şeyh*. Shaykh al-Islam: The head of the hierarchy of the doctors of Muslim canon law, tradition and theology. Tr. Şeyhülislam.

c98013e1-9336-5b90-9d71-2658cca1e0ca.definition: (Pl. *shurafa*) Descendant of the Prophet Muhammad. See also *sayyed*.

288b2150-8838-5cdf-8779-d98b7d476915.definition: The Sira are the prophetic biographies.  In addition to what is written in the Quran and Hadith, the sira also provide information on Muhammed's life and the early period of Islam.

8d51b0ae-13b3-5a75-acf3-79e63e2bd891.definition: An arch placed diagonally at each corner of a square and filled decoratively with a variety of methods, providing the transition from the cubical walls to the sphere of the dome.

b68f8c65-978e-5a31-bb68-5994ae43ec75.definition: A Muslim acetic and mystic who represents the mystical aspect of Islam.

ddce3372-545d-5166-8dfc-c8bb72ab9fe8.definition: An Islamic mystical or ascetic order. Derived from *suf*, wool, which is the fabric in which devotees (*sufi*) clothe themselves. Fr. *soufisme*.

aea62142-bf4f-5655-8c52-b1e856151ce7.definition: Honorary title used by independent sovereigns (in particular Ottomans and Seljuks) whose authority, however, does not question the nominal superiority recognised to the ruling caliph.

f21a9ff0-ae8f-5ff9-be18-36b4a4db6794.definition: State or territories that are ruled by a sultan. Sultan is a title given to the ruler of such a place.

811580e5-c0b8-5c27-8c10-3a3a36bee143.definition: Literally “tradition”. For Orthodox Islam, the group of traditions of the Prophet in which legal advisers and theologians find support and foundations to establish the content of Islamic law arising from the Qur’an. Sunni: Follower of Sunna. Sunnis are divided into four schools: Hanafi, Hanbali, Maliki, Shafi’i. Sunnism: a political and religious system opposed to Shi‘ism. See also Fiqh, Shi’a.

5c212d06-15e4-5918-a02d-bb0ef2c59fe1.definition: Chapter of the Qur’an. There are 114 surahs in the Qur’an. Tr. Sure.

665383f5-4a15-5f32-8010-a19d807b45a5.definition: Guestroom at a mosque for itinerant dervishes and other travellers. From the AH 10th / AD 16th century *tabhanes* became part of the mosque’s prayer hall.

b9925565-dd1a-5d2a-b600-c734be2f3586.definition: Factions or groups. The term usually refers to the disintegration of Muslim Spain into several smaller kingdoms during the 5th/11th century.

1ad49aeb-c4a6-56fa-a5db-9635fe80d767.definition: From Tr. *tekke*, literally “place where food is served free of charge”. Centre where dervishes meet, worship and live. Architectural type introduced by the Ottomans. See also *imaret*, *khan*qah, *zawiya*.

cc2bbcf5-54f0-5959-a72b-231b955a7d9c.definition:
One of the six main styles of calligraphy developed in Persia in the AH 9th / AD 15th century. Used especially for official correspondence, it is characterised by fine lines with no vowel. Tr. *talik*. See also *nasta’liq*, calligraphy.  
  
Taliq is characterised by an unauthodox use of ligatures, which connect letters on the left that typically wouldn't be joined. It features descending strokes that form loops, rounded letter shapes with pronounced variations in letter spacing, wide spacing between lines, as well as lines that ascend from right to left.

9b57e731-19ab-55da-8b80-25d31d0f41c3.definition:
Arabic: “one-third”. A style of calligraphy named after the size of the pen used. The prolongation of its letters allow for very complex decorative compositions. It was used in calligraphy, books and civil and religious architecture. From the AH 12th / AD 18th century it was widely used in panels particular to Ottoman art. Fr. *toulouth*. Tr. *sülüs*.  
  
The thuluth script, a medieval Islamic calligraphic style, features an alphabet written in a distinctive manner. The name "thuluth" (Arabic for "one-third") refers to the principle that each letter's form encompasses a slope of about one-third of its size. This script is both spacious and refined, characterized by its cursive nature. During the medieval period, thuluth script found its place on mosque embellishments.  
Functionally, thuluth script assumed some of the roles initially held by the early Kufic script. It was employed for crafting headings for suras (chapters) of the Qurʾan, religious inscriptions, princely titles, and inscriptions of importance. Additionally, from the 13th century AD (597-700 AH) onwards, it was favoured for producing large copies of the Qurʾan.

a054eff3-ab33-572b-8c6c-47a7d300c111.definition: First used for embroidered inscriptions on textiles, this term became synonymous with textile robes with inscriptions giving the ruler’s name and the workshop where the textiles were made. Such robes were presented by the caliph to people who were to be honoured. Dar al-tiraz: royal textile factories supervised by the court.

ce2219af-ca75-5d6e-a3b1-280a9ea04fbc.definition: Mausoleum, tomb, private burial place, sometimes with a crypt below, an architectural practice introduced by the Turks. Tr. *kümbet*, a monumental tomb, usually covered with a dome hidden under a spire. See also *darih*, *maqam*, *mashhad*, *qubba*.

5cc4d556-5ce6-575d-a50b-a403e6c59d4f.definition: A headdress consisting of a long scarf wound round the head or a smaller, underlying hat. Turbans vary in shape, colour, and size.

38031924-6b4f-5fb1-9337-c0222f9b16d2.definition: Endowment in perpetuity, usually of land or property, from which the revenue was reserved for the upkeep of religious foundations. *waqfiyya*: the deed of endowment of a *waqf*. Tr. *vakıf*, *vakfiye*. See also *habus*.

9d0320cb-1068-5d1a-bb89-97a0628cb0f4.definition: Trading establishment with lodgings for merchants. See also *caravanserai*, *funduq*, *khan*.

cc1e247a-53d7-5c70-9399-89357963e5cf.definition: A style in Ottoman art which uses Chinoiserie decorations. The designs incorporate stylised lotus blossoms, buds and leaves in decorative scrolls. Hatayi is derived from Chatay in China. See also Chinoiserie.

bcebf34c-f01e-5220-896e-b24e7d5c3220.definition: Hostel for merchants and their pack animals, a store for merchandise, a commercial centre. See also *caravanserai*, *khan*, *wikala*.

76676210-58c4-5de1-89e6-594e4175ceac.definition: Establishment for religious teaching dedicated to preparing men to become *shaykhs*, which includes the shrine of a saint and built where he was born or lived. In Turkey also a small *tekke*, a hospice for dervishes and travellers. See also *khanqah*, *tekke*, *takiyya*.
